paper.title: Provable Model-based Nonlinear Bandit and Reinforcement Learning: Shelve Optimism, Embrace Virtual Curvature

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear bandit problem with deterministic reward (local regret)
unmapped: Regret is local regret: compared with the worst (eps_g, eps_h)-approximate local maximum of the true reward
Realizable known model class eta(theta,a) in [0,1], actions in R^{d_A}; complexity measured by sequential Rademacher complexity of an induced loss class
Reward, gradient and Hessian Lipschitz (Assumption 2.1) with constants zeta_g, zeta_h, zeta_3; algorithm uses zeta_g, zeta_h to set clipping levels
Algorithm queries finite differences (several infinitesimally perturbed actions per round) to estimate gradient/Hessian projections
settings.definition_quote: We consider deterministic nonlinear bandit problem with continuous actions. Let \theta \in \Theta be the parameter that specifies the bandit instance, a\in \R^{d_A} the action, and \eta(\theta,a)\in [0,1] the reward function. ... realizability assumption that \theta^\star\in \Theta.

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear deterministic bandit: convergence to approximate local maximum action
unmapped: Goal: some played action a_t is an (eps, 6 sqrt(zeta_3 eps))-approximate local maximum
Lipschitz gradient/Hessian assumptions; sequential Rademacher complexity bounded by sqrt(R(Theta) T polylog T)
settings.definition_quote: The sample complexity for converging to approximate local maxima is defined to be the minimal number of steps T such that there exists t\in [T] where a_t is an (\epsilon_g,\epsilon_h) approximate local maximum with probability at least 1-\delta.

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic linear bandit with finite (or sparse) model class, unit-ball actions
unmapped: Parameter class Theta is a known finite subset of the unit sphere (or s-sparse unit vectors)
settings.definition_quote: Consider the problem with action set \calA = \{a\in \R^{d}: \|a\|_2\le 1 \} and finite model class \Theta \subset \{\theta\in \R^d : \|\theta\|_2=1\}. Suppose the reward is linear, that is, \eta(\theta,a) = \langle \theta, a\rangle.

unmapped: Reward eta((W1,W2),a)=W2 sigma(W1 a) - ||a||^2/2 with ||W1||_{1,inf}<=1, ||W2||_1<=1 and activation with bounded derivatives up to third order
Local regret vs approximate local maxima (global regret when network is input-concave)
settings.definition_quote: let \eta((W_1,W_2),a)=W_2\sigma(W_1 a)-\frac{1}{2}\|a\|_2^2 ... Let the model hypothesis space be \Theta=\{(W_1,W_2):\|W_1\|_{1,\infty}\le 1, \|W_2\|_1\le 1\}

settings.name_in_paper: Model-based RL with deterministic nonlinear dynamics and stochastic parameterized policies
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Episodic reinforcement learning (finite-horizon MDP with deterministic dynamics), not a bandit problem
unmapped: Local regret over policy parameters; Lipschitz assumptions 2.1, 4.1, 4.2; trajectories observed
settings.definition_quote: We consider finite horizon Markov decision process (MDP) with deterministic dynamics, defined by a tuple <T,r,H,mu_1> ...

settings.name_in_paper: One-layer ReLU neural net bandit, deterministic reward (lower bound)
unmapped: Reward eta((w,b),a)=ReLU(<w,a>+b), actions in unit ball of R^d
settings.definition_quote: the reward function can be written in the form of \eta((w,b),a)=\mathrm{ReLU}(\dotp{w}{a}+b).

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic linear reward on the sphere with two-layer NN hypothesis class (UCB lower bound)
unmapped: Ground truth linear on S^{d-1}; hypothesis class is two-layer networks of width d
settings.definition_quote: Consider the case where the ground-truth reward function is linear: \dotp{\thetas}{a} and the action set is a\in S^{d-1}. If the hypothesis is chosen to be two-layer neural network with width d

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit on the sphere with Gaussian noise, finite hypothesis {e_1..e_d} (lower bound)
unmapped: Goal: find a (0.1,1)-approximate second-order stationary point
settings.definition_quote: Our hard instance is linear bandit with hypothesis \Theta=\{e_1,\cdots,e_d\}, action space \calA=S^{d-1} and i.i.d. standard Gaussian noise.

algorithms.name: ViOlin (Virtual Ascent with Online Model Learner, bandit)
UCB with tightest upper confidence bound (deterministic environment)

symbols.R_T: sequential Rademacher complexity of the loss class in Eq. (bandit-loss)
symbols.zeta_h: bound on reward Hessian spectral norm

source.label: thm:bandit-main
source.quote: Let $\src_T$ be the sequential Rademacher complexity of the family of the losses defined in Eq.~\eqref{equ:bandit-loss}. Let $C_1=2+\gasup/\hasup$. Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:lipschitz}, for any $\epsilon\le \mintwo{1}{\tasup/16},$ we can bound the $(\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon})$-local regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} from above by \E[\reg_{\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon}}(T)] \le (1+C_1\sqrt{4T\src_T})\max(4\hasup\epsilon^{-2},\sqrt{\tasup}\epsilon^{-3/2}).

results.notes: Quantity is (eps, 6 sqrt(zeta_3 eps))-local regret, compared with the worst approximate local maximum; no matching vocabulary so recorded as 'other'. epsilon is the local-maximum tolerance.

symbols.R_Theta: complexity parameter R(Theta) with sequential Rademacher complexity <= sqrt(R(Theta) T polylog T)

conditions: sequential Rademacher complexity of the loss bounded by sqrt(R(Theta) T polylog(T))
Assumption 2.1; zeta_g, zeta_h, zeta_3 treated as constants

source.label: thm:ban-action-space
source.quote: Suppose the sequential Rademacher complexity of the loss function (defined in Eq.~\eqref{equ:bandit-loss}) is bounded by $\sqrt{R(\Theta)T\polylog(T)}.$ When $T\gtrsim R(\Theta)\epsilon^{-8}\polylog(R(\Theta),1/\epsilon)$, if we run Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} for $T$ steps, there exists $t\in [T]$ such that $a_t\in \sosp_{\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon}}$ with probability at least $0.5$.

symbols.N_Theta: size |Theta| of the finite model class

conditions: finite model class on the unit sphere

source.number: Section 3.1 (Linear bandit with finite model class)
source.quote: We claim that the expected (global) regret is bounded by $\bigO\pbra{T^{15/16}\pbra{\log|\Theta|}^{1/16}}$.

results.notes: Stated as a claim in the instantiation section, proved in Appendix B.5; not a numbered theorem. Dimension-free. Same rate claimed for deterministic logistic bandits.

source.number: Section 3.1 (Linear bandit with sparse or structured model vectors)
source.quote: we claim that the global regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} is $\E[\reg(T)]=\tildeO\pbra{T^{15/16}s^{1/16}}.$

results.notes: Claim via discretization into (dT)^{O(s)} points; hides log(dT) factors.

source.label: thm:two-layer
source.quote: Under the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:bandit-main} with Assumption~\ref{assumption:two-layer}, the local regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} running on two-layer neural networks can be bounded by $\tildeO\pbra{\epsilon^{-2}T^{3/4}}.$

conditions: neural network is input concave (e.g. W2 nonpositive, sigma monotone convex)

source.label: thm:two-layer
source.quote: In addition, if the neural network is input concave, then the global regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:ban} is bounded by $\tildeO\pbra{T^{7/8}}.$

symbols.R_T_dyn: sequential Rademacher complexity of the dynamics loss in Eq. (rl-loss)

source.label: thm:rl-main
source.quote: Under Assumption~\ref{assumption:lipschitz}-\ref{assumption:RL-smoothness}, for any $\epsilon\le \mintwo{1}{\frac{\tasup}{16}},$ we can bound the  $(\epsilon,6\sqrt{\tasup\epsilon})$-regret of Alg.~\ref{alg:rl} by \E[\reg(T)] \le (1+C_1\sqrt{2c_1T\srcrl_T})\max(2\hasup\epsilon^{-2},\sqrt{\tasup}\epsilon^{-3/2}).

results.notes: RL local regret; out of scope. Instantiated on Example 4.3 to O(poly(sigma,1/sigma,H,L_r) T^{3/4} log|Theta|^{1/4} eps^{-2}).

conditions: one-layer ReLU network reward class, deterministic

source.label: thm:lowerbound-sample-comp
source.quote: When the function class is chosen to be one-layer neural networks with ReLU activation, the minimax sample complexity is $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-(d-2)}).$

results.notes: Proof derives minimax regret Omega(T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}) and converts via regret-to-sample-complexity reduction.

conditions: one-layer ReLU network reward class, deterministic
results.notes: Intermediate statement inside the proof of Theorem 5.1; reward deterministic so pseudo- and expected regret coincide.

conditions: applies to the UCB algorithm with the tightest upper confidence bound

source.label: thm:lowerbound-optimism
source.quote: Consider the case where the ground-truth reward function is linear: $\dotp{\thetas}{a}$ and the action set is $a\in S^{d-1}.$ If the hypothesis is chosen to be two-layer neural network with width $d$, UCB algorithm with tightest upper confidence bound  suffers exponential sample complexity .

results.notes: Theorem says 'exponential'; Omega(2^d) is from the proof.

source.label: thm:lowerbound-stochastic
source.quote: There exists an bandit problem with stochastic reward and hypothesis class with size $\log |\Theta|=\tildeO\pbra{1}$, such that any algorithm requires $\Omega\pbra{d}$ sample to find a $(0.1,1)$-approximate second order stationary point with probability at least $3/4.$

results.notes: Target is a (0.1,1)-approximate second-order stationary point.
